COLORS LESSON · COLORS & SHADES · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Grey — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the color grey: elephant grey, cloud grey, the calmest color in the deck.

What is this?

Grey is a color — the color of the elephant, the cloud, the rock and the koala on the card. It is black and white mixed: the color between night and snow.

What does it mean?

Grey is the quiet color: clouds before rain, elephants padding through the savanna, stones on the path. When your child names grey, they are naming calm and heavy and soft-at-the-same-time.

What does the child need to know?

The child needs to: say "grey", meet grey on two animals (elephant, koala), one sky thing (cloud) and one ground thing (rock), and hear BOTH spellings — grey and gray.

Why this matters

Grey is the only card in the deck with a spelling story: the US writes GRAY, the UK writes GREY. Same color, two spellings — meeting both now prevents the later "which is right?" wobble.

What it teaches

Vocabulary plus a spelling note most preschools skip, heavy-versus-light reasoning (heavy elephant, light cloud — same color), and slow-fast movement vocabulary.

Words to learn

greygrayelephantcloudrockkoalastompfloatheavygentle

Say this to your child

“"Grey! The elephant is grey, the cloud is grey, the rock is grey, the koala is grey. Grey is the calm color. Stomp like an elephant — slooow and heavy. Now float like a cloud… soft and light."”

Step by step

  1. Point and name: elephant — grey, cloud — grey, rock — grey, koala — grey. Two animals, one sky, one ground.
  2. Heavy and light: the elephant weighs as much as a car; the cloud weighs almost nothing (it is made of tiny water drops). Same color, opposite weights — grey does not pick sides.
  3. Spell it both ways: say "grey" while tracing a G in the air, then the US way — "gray" — same word, different clothes. Both are right; families pick their own.
  4. The stomp and the float: stomp slow and heavy like the elephant (five grey stomps), then float to the sofa like the cloud. Heavy, then light.
  5. Koala close: yawn like the sleepy koala, hug like one too — koalas hug trees for naps. Choose a chair-tree. Nap optional, yawn mandatory.

Look closer at the picture

The elephant is the biggest land animal alive, and the koala is the sleepiest — it naps up to twenty hours a day. Grey is home to both the giant and the napper.

Ask your child

"Which grey animal is the biggest on land?" (elephant) "Which grey thing floats in the sky?" (cloud) "Which spelling does OUR family use — grey or gray?" (both are right!)

What your child can say or do

Your child might stomp everywhere announcing "ELEPHANT COMING" or yawn theatrically like the koala at bedtime. The koala yawn is a gift at tuck-in time — use it.

Out in the real world

Real elephants are grey; real clouds are white-grey-rainbow depending on the day. Koalas live in Australia and are NOT bears — the koala square’s grown-up fact, delivered with respect.

Try it together

Cloud watch: lie on the rug, look at the ceiling or the sky, and call the shapes — "that one is an elephant cloud, that one is a turtle cloud." Grey spotting, imagination, zero mess.

Understanding check

Ask: "what color is the elephant?" (grey) "Can you say it the US way?" (gray!) "Show me a heavy stomp, then a floaty float." (the room says it worked)

This lesson pairs with the Grey flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Colors & Shades.
